introduction: This spec defines the PAT Permission Updates feature for apikit, which adds three new API endpoints and corresponding CLI commands to replace, add, and remove permissions on an existing Personal Access Token (PAT) in-place, avoiding unnecessary secret rotation.

glossary.DoRequest: The HTTP helper function used by CLI commands to make authenticated HTTP requests to the apikit server, following the pattern established in tokens.go.
glossary.GetAuthInfo: The auth middleware helper that retrieves the AuthInfo (credential type, permissions) for the current request from the Echo context.
glossary.GetUserID: The auth middleware helper that retrieves the authenticated user's ID from the Echo context.
glossary.NewPermissionRegistry: The constructor function that initializes the PermissionRegistry with all built-in permissions; tokens:write is added here.
glossary.PAT: Personal Access Token — a user-created, fine-grained credential that grants scoped access to API resources via resource_type:action permission pairs.
glossary.PATHandler: The Go struct in internal/handlers/pat.go that owns all PAT-related HTTP handler methods and route registration.
glossary.PATResponse: The JSON response shape returned by PAT endpoints, defined in internal/handlers/pat.go, including fields such as id, name, permissions, revoked_at, and expires_at.
glossary.PermissionRegistry: The registry of all valid built-in permissions in the system, used to validate permission strings supplied by callers.
glossary.RegisterRoutes: The method on PATHandler that registers all PAT HTTP routes with the Echo router; modified in-place by this spec to add the three new permission endpoints.
glossary.RequirePermission: The auth middleware helper that checks whether the authenticated caller holds a specific permission, returning HTTP 403 if not.
glossary.UpdatePATPermissionsRequest: The Go struct representing the JSON request body for PUT, PATCH, and DELETE on /user/tokens/:token_id/permissions, containing a Permissions []string field.
glossary.auth_middleware: The upstream spec (spec 05) that defines RequirePermission, GetAuthInfo, GetUserID, and PermissionRegistry.
glossary.auto-revoke: The behavior of setting revoked_at to the current UTC timestamp when a replace or remove operation results in a token with zero permissions.
glossary.cli_user_commands: The upstream spec (spec 15) that defines the CLI token command registration pattern, parsePermissions helper, and DoRequest HTTP call pattern.
glossary.db.WithTx: The database helper that executes a function within a SQLite transaction, ensuring atomicity of read-modify-write operations.
glossary.expires_at: The timestamp column on the pats table that, when non-NULL and in the past, indicates the token has expired.
glossary.parsePermissions: The CLI helper function in tokens.go that splits a comma-separated permissions string and trims whitespace, reused by the three new CLI commands.
glossary.pat_lifecycle: The upstream spec (spec 09) that defines PATHandler, PATResponse, and RegisterRoutes.
glossary.pats: The SQLite table that stores Personal Access Token records, including a permissions TEXT column containing a JSON-serialized array.
glossary.privilege escalation: The rule that a PAT-authenticated caller cannot grant permissions to a token that the caller's own PAT does not already hold.
glossary.resource_type:action: The format for permission strings, consisting of a resource type and an action separated by exactly one colon (e.g., users:read, orgs:write).
glossary.revoked_at: The timestamp column on the pats table that, when non-NULL, indicates the token has been revoked.
glossary.token_id: The URL path parameter identifying the target PAT for permission modification operations.
glossary.tokens:manage: An existing built-in permission that grants the ability to create, revoke, and modify PAT permissions in-place. It is a superset of tokens:write.
glossary.tokens:write: A new built-in permission (the 7th) that grants the ability to modify PAT permissions in-place. It is a strict subset of tokens:manage.

user_story.goal: have a dedicated tokens:write permission that grants in-place PAT permission modification without full tokens:manage access
user_story.benefit: operators can grant minimal privilege to callers that only need to modify token permissions, not create or revoke tokens

acceptance_criteria.action: register tokens:write as the 7th built-in permission alongside the existing 6 permissions
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: returns a PermissionRegistry containing exactly 7 built-in permissions including tokens:write
acceptance_criteria.trigger: NewPermissionRegistry() is called

acceptance_criteria.action: treat tokens:write as a strict subset of tokens:manage — a PAT holding tokens:manage satisfies any OR-check that includes tokens:write

edge_cases.action: panic or return an error at startup to prevent duplicate registration
edge_cases.return_contract: returns an error or panics with a descriptive message indicating duplicate permission registration
edge_cases.error_condition: tokens:write is registered more than once in NewPermissionRegistry()

acceptance_criteria.action: check that each permission in the new set that is NOT already present on the target token is also present in the caller's own PAT permissions; if any new permission is not held by the caller, reject the request
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: returns HTTP 403 with JSON body {error: "cannot grant permission: <permission>"} for the first escalating permission found

acceptance_criteria.condition: the caller is authenticated via PAT

correctness_properties.title: Replace is idempotent for identical permission sets
correctness_properties.for_any: valid token_id and non-empty permissions array P
correctness_properties.invariant: calling PUT /user/tokens/:token_id/permissions with P twice in sequence results in the same PATResponse as calling it once

correctness_properties.title: Add never introduces duplicate permissions
correctness_properties.for_any: valid token_id and any sequence of PATCH requests with overlapping permissions
correctness_properties.invariant: the permissions array in the pats table never contains duplicate entries after any number of add operations

correctness_properties.title: Remove is idempotent
correctness_properties.for_any: valid token_id and permissions array P
correctness_properties.invariant: calling DELETE /user/tokens/:token_id/permissions with P twice in sequence results in the same PATResponse as calling it once

correctness_properties.title: Auto-revocation is triggered exactly when permissions become empty
correctness_properties.for_any: any replace or remove operation on a non-revoked, non-expired token
correctness_properties.invariant: revoked_at is set if and only if the resulting permissions array is empty

correctness_properties.title: User isolation — callers cannot modify other users' tokens
correctness_properties.for_any: any permission modification request with a token_id belonging to a different user
correctness_properties.invariant: the handler returns HTTP 404 and makes no changes to the pats table

correctness_properties.title: Privilege escalation is enforced for PAT callers on replace and add
correctness_properties.for_any: any PAT-authenticated caller and any permission P not held by the caller's PAT
correctness_properties.invariant: a replace or add request that would grant P to the target token is rejected with HTTP 403

correctness_properties.title: Revoked and expired tokens cannot be modified
correctness_properties.for_any: any token with non-null revoked_at or with expires_at in the past
correctness_properties.invariant: all three permission modification endpoints return HTTP 400 and make no changes to the pats table

correctness_properties.title: All stored permissions are registered and validly formatted
correctness_properties.for_any: any successful replace or add operation
correctness_properties.invariant: every permission string in the resulting pats.permissions JSON array is registered in the PermissionRegistry and contains exactly one colon

correctness_properties.title: tokens:write is the 7th built-in permission
correctness_properties.invariant: the returned PermissionRegistry contains exactly 7 built-in permissions including tokens:write

execution_paths.title: Replace PAT permissions via API — happy path

steps.action: sends PUT /user/tokens/:token_id/permissions with Authorization: Bearer <PAT> and JSON body {permissions: ["users:read", "orgs:read"]}
validates the Bearer token, extracts AuthInfo and user ID from the pats table, and injects them into the Echo context
checks that the caller holds tokens:write or tokens:manage; returns HTTP 403 if neither is held
parses and validates the UpdatePATPermissionsRequest body; returns HTTP 400 for malformed JSON or missing permissions field
queries the pats table by token_id AND user_id; returns HTTP 404 if not found
checks revoked_at and expires_at guards; returns HTTP 400 if token is revoked or expired
validates each permission string format and registry membership; returns HTTP 400 for invalid or unknown permissions
checks privilege escalation for PAT callers — verifies each new permission is held by the caller; returns HTTP 403 if not
executes UPDATE on the pats table within db.WithTx, setting permissions to the new JSON-serialized array
returns HTTP 200 with PATResponse showing the updated permissions set

execution_paths.title: Replace PAT permissions with empty array — auto-revocation

steps.action: sends PUT /user/tokens/:token_id/permissions with JSON body {permissions: []}
validates the Bearer token and injects AuthInfo into the Echo context
passes permission check, parses body, looks up token, passes revocation and expiry guards
detects empty permissions array — skips format/registry validation and privilege escalation
executes UPDATE on the pats table within db.WithTx, setting permissions to [] and revoked_at to current UTC timestamp
returns HTTP 200 with PATResponse where revoked_at is set

execution_paths.title: Add permissions via API — happy path

steps.action: sends PATCH /user/tokens/:token_id/permissions with Authorization: Bearer <PAT> and JSON body {permissions: ["orgs:write"]}
validates the Bearer token and injects AuthInfo and user ID into the Echo context
checks that the caller holds tokens:write or tokens:manage
parses and validates the UpdatePATPermissionsRequest body; rejects if permissions is absent, null, or empty
queries the pats table by token_id AND user_id; returns HTTP 404 if not found
checks revoked_at and expires_at guards
validates each permission string format and registry membership
checks privilege escalation for PAT callers
computes the merged permissions set by appending only permissions not already present
executes UPDATE on the pats table within db.WithTx, setting permissions to the merged JSON-serialized array
returns HTTP 200 with PATResponse showing the merged permissions set

execution_paths.title: Remove all permissions via API — auto-revocation

steps.action: sends DELETE /user/tokens/:token_id/permissions with JSON body {permissions: ["users:read"]} where users:read is the only permission on the token
validates the Bearer token and injects AuthInfo into the Echo context
checks that the caller holds tokens:write or tokens:manage
parses and validates the UpdatePATPermissionsRequest body
queries the pats table by token_id AND user_id
checks revoked_at and expires_at guards
validates format of each permission string; silently ignores unregistered permissions
computes the resulting permissions set after removal — detects it is empty
executes UPDATE on the pats table within db.WithTx, setting permissions to [] and revoked_at to current UTC timestamp
returns HTTP 200 with PATResponse where revoked_at is set

execution_paths.title: akc tokens replace CLI — end-to-end flow

steps.action: runs akc tokens replace <token_id> --permissions users:read,orgs:read
calls parsePermissions on the --permissions flag value to produce ["users:read", "orgs:read"]
calls DoRequest with method PUT, path /user/tokens/<token_id>/permissions, and UpdatePATPermissionsRequest body
validates the Bearer token from CLI config and injects AuthInfo
processes the request through all validation, escalation, and database update steps
returns HTTP 200 with PATResponse
prints the PATResponse JSON to stdout; if revoked_at is non-null, prints revocation warning to stderr
observes the updated token state in stdout output

execution_paths.title: Full PAT permission lifecycle — create, add, replace, remove

steps.action: sends POST /user/tokens to create a PAT with permissions ["users:read"]
creates the PAT and returns PATResponse with permissions ["users:read"]
sends PATCH /user/tokens/:token_id/permissions with {permissions: ["orgs:read"]}
merges permissions and returns PATResponse with permissions ["users:read", "orgs:read"]
sends PUT /user/tokens/:token_id/permissions with {permissions: ["orgs:write"]}
replaces permissions and returns PATResponse with permissions ["orgs:write"]
sends DELETE /user/tokens/:token_id/permissions with {permissions: ["orgs:write"]}
removes all permissions, sets revoked_at, and returns PATResponse with empty permissions and non-null revoked_at
observes the token is now revoked via the revoked_at field in the final PATResponse

error_handling.condition: permissions field is absent or null in the request body
error_handling.behavior: return HTTP 400 with JSON body {error: "permissions are required"}

error_handling.condition: permissions field is an empty array for PATCH or DELETE
error_handling.behavior: return HTTP 400 with JSON body {error: "permissions are required"}

error_handling.condition: a permission string does not contain exactly one colon
error_handling.behavior: return HTTP 400 with JSON body {error: "invalid permission format: <permission>"}

error_handling.condition: a permission string is validly formatted but not registered in the PermissionRegistry (replace or add only)
error_handling.behavior: return HTTP 400 with JSON body {error: "unknown permission: <permission>"}

error_handling.condition: the target token's revoked_at is non-NULL
error_handling.behavior: return HTTP 400 with JSON body {error: "token is revoked"}

error_handling.condition: the target token's expires_at is non-NULL and in the past
error_handling.behavior: return HTTP 400 with JSON body {error: "token is expired"}

error_handling.condition: the caller is authenticated via PAT and holds neither tokens:write nor tokens:manage
error_handling.behavior: return HTTP 403 with JSON body {error: "insufficient permissions"}

error_handling.condition: a PAT caller attempts to grant a permission not held by their own PAT (replace or add only)
error_handling.behavior: return HTTP 403 with JSON body {error: "cannot grant permission: <permission>"}

error_handling.condition: the token_id does not exist in the pats table or belongs to a different user
error_handling.behavior: return HTTP 404 with JSON body {error: "token not found"}

error_handling.condition: the request body is malformed JSON
error_handling.behavior: return HTTP 400 with JSON body {error: "invalid request body"}

error_handling.condition: a database error occurs during the UPDATE operation
error_handling.behavior: roll back the db.WithTx transaction and return HTTP 500 with JSON body {error: "internal server error"}

error_handling.condition: the request arrives without authentication credentials
error_handling.behavior: auth middleware rejects the request with HTTP 401 before the handler is invoked
